Q925.L1t: Future interests such as executory interests are interests that take effect in possession only after some later event occurs.
Q925.L2t: An executory interest is a future interest held by a transferee that cuts short a preceding fee simple when a stated condition occurs.
Q925.L3t: The Greenacre condition could be triggered by anyone at any time in the indefinite future, so it might not vest within a life in being plus 21 years, whereas the Blackacre condition turns only on Associate's own conduct and must resolve within her lifetime.
Q925.L4t: Friend keeps Greenacre because Betty's executory interest in it is void under the Rule Against Perpetuities, while Betty takes Blackacre because her interest there is valid and Associate's drinking triggered it.
Q925.L2f: An executory interest is a type of reversion that always stays with the original grantor rather than passing to a third party.
Q925.L3f: The Rule Against Perpetuities does not apply to a gift over to the grantor's own heir, so both conditions are valid and both were triggered by the drinking.
Q925.L4f: Betty takes both Greenacre and Blackacre, because the drinking on each parcel triggered her executory interest.

Q933.L1t: The human mouth is home to bacteria, fungi, viruses and protozoa that live together as part of the body's normal flora.
Q933.L2t: The oral cavity has one of the most diverse microbial communities in the body, and many of its members live in biofilms such as dental plaque.
Q933.L3t: Culture-based and molecular surveys of the oral cavity have catalogued several hundred distinct microbial types, which is clearly more than a hundred but fewer than four hundred.
Q933.L4t: The mouth may be colonized by roughly three hundred and fifty different types of microorganisms.
Q933.L2f: Nearly all microbes in the mouth float freely in saliva and cannot attach to tooth surfaces or form biofilms.
Q933.L3f: Comprehensive surveys of the mouth have found only a modest total that tops out at one-tenth of a thousand types, and molecular methods have added essentially nothing to that count.
Q933.L4f: The mouth may be colonized by about one hundred different types of microorganisms.
